absent: Legitimacy predicate for namespace enumeration and scoped user namespace listing path.
Layouts and lifetime of namespace common object, tree roots, unified root, and listing request descriptors.
Reader guard and reference counting contracts for namespace objects.
Layouts of parallel private descriptor, shared parallel data, shell, instance, reorder collection, and serial queue.
Semantics of parallel versus serial callbacks, callback CPU affinity, and multithread chunking and completion.
Workqueue, pool, pool workqueue, worker, and attribute structure layouts and scheduling state machines.
Pool hashing, NUMA pod selection, identifier allocation bounds, and commit path for attribute changes.
Error handling for request copy, attribute allocation, and CPU mask operations beyond the status codes shown.

findings.text: Parallel submission service accepts a shell handle plus a private job descriptor and a callback placement hint, validates readiness, normalizes placement, assigns ordering state, and either queues background work or completes inline, distinguishing invalid use from busy reset state.
Serial staging service accepts a finished parallel job and either parks it in ordered per CPU storage or drives dispatch of the next contiguous run.
Targeted queueing service requests execution of a work item on a chosen CPU with at most once pending semantics while preserving interrupt masking across the check and enqueue.
Attribute application service updates an unbound workqueue from a caller supplied attribute set under global serialization.
Attribute release service disposes an attribute object and its associated masks while tolerating a null argument.

Namespace listing entry requires a zeroed flags word, enforces a fixed upper bound of one million [CITED] on requested count, checks caller buffer accessibility, copies a request descriptor, and selects between scoped and global enumeration.
Work wrapper layout combines an embedded schedulable element with a linkage element for free pool membership and an opaque payload pointer.
Multithread job control layout combines mutual exclusion state with a completion signal, a back link to the job, total versus finished worker tallies, and a chunk sizing field.
File scope holds a pointer anchoring work item storage together with a dedicated lock protecting pool membership.
On stack storage indicator has numeric value one [CITED]; when set the embedded work element uses on stack initialization rather than generic initialization.

Identifier lookup provides lower bound search over either a type partitioned ordered index or a unified ordered index under a reader guard, returning a live reference only when the located object remains active and null otherwise including unknown type.
List traversal abstraction selects between partitioned and unified linkage depending on whether a type root is present, offering first, next, and end detection usable under read side protection.

Enumeration offers resumable ordered export of identifiers with single type filtering when exactly one type bit is set and unified view otherwise, starting after a supplied predecessor when present and reporting count placed while skipping entries rejected by a legitimacy predicate.

Submission assigns increasing ordering labels under mutual exclusion and normalizes callback placement to an allowed set with deterministic fallback when the hint is outside, while serial dispatch advances expected labels and associated CPUs together with reset to the initial CPU on wrap.
Reorder staging keeps per CPU collections sorted by ordering label using wrap aware difference comparison and distinguishes the immediately dispatchable head from deferred entries.

Effective CPU selection intersects requested masks with the allowed unbound set and falls back to the full allowed set when disjoint, with further sanitization against possible CPUs for stored user masks.
Pool workqueue construction obtains or creates a matching unbound pool then allocates the queue object on the pool node, releasing the pool reference if allocation fails.

Multithread startup preallocates helper work items for all but the participating caller, initializing each for a common helper entry and chaining them for later execution, stopping early when the pool is exhausted.
Bulk release helper returns a caller supplied chain of work items to the free pool under protection while tolerating an empty chain.
Parallelism restriction builds fresh attributes, constrains workers to the instance parallel mask, applies the result, and always releases the temporary attributes.
Queueing is idempotent with respect to concurrent attempts: only the transition from non pending to pending while enabled triggers actual insertion.

Job lifecycle progresses from submission with shared state reference acquisition through parallel execution, ordered staging, serial queueing, callback invocation, and batched reference release that ultimately frees masks and per CPU areas when the final reference drops.

Attribute change moves from validation and context preparation through commitment to cleanup, with ordered queues temporarily suspending new execution until prior items drain and with failure during preparation releasing all partially built state.

Unbound pool lifecycle moves from hash lookup or node aware creation with identifier assignment and initial worker spawn through shared reuse to final release that unhashes, quiesces management ownership, retires idle workers, cancels timers, and defers reclamation.

A dedicated global spin lock protects membership in the reusable work item pool; acquisition when queueing and return after parallel execution both occur with that lock held, using bottom half safe forms on submission paths and explicit bottom half management on worker paths.

Distinct fine grained locks protect each per CPU reorder collection and each serial queue; reorder inspection and mutation hold the reorder lock while serial list append and worker wake hold the serial lock, with the serial worker splicing the pending list under the lock and invoking callbacks after release.

Shell state is observed under short read side bottom half protection while longer term stability relies on reference counting on shared parallel state acquired at submission and released in bulk after serial callbacks.

A global pool mutex serializes attribute preparation, pool acquisition, and pool teardown with helpers asserting its ownership; pool specific locking with interrupt masking protects individual pool workqueue reference changes.
Worker attachment changes require a dedicated attach mutex; detachment with affinity relaxation and list removal occurs under it while pool accounting updates additionally require the pool lock.

Enumeration temporarily leaves read side protection to copy each identifier to caller memory, preserving the previously validated item across the copy and managing references on fault, then re enters protection before advancing.

Pool teardown refuses to retire workers that still have active work or scheduled state or that are not marked idle, and it clears cached last woken references to avoid use after free during observability.
When the reusable work pool is empty at submission the parallel function runs synchronously in the submitter rather than being queued, preserving progress without additional queueing.
